monitorForm.name: name
monitorForm.pushHint: pingtxt gives this monitor a secret URL. Call it at the end of every run of your job: the monitor goes down when no call arrives within the expected period plus the grace time. The URL is shown after saving.
monitorForm.dockerHint: Checked on the docker engine of each selected location: the hub or agent needs access to /var/run/docker.sock (or DOCKER_HOST). With docker, mount it with -v /var/run/docker.sock:/var/run/docker.sock:ro.
monitorForm.grpcHint: grpc:// for plaintext, grpcs:// for TLS. The path is the service name to check; leave it out to check the whole server.
monitorForm.udpPayloadHint: Sent to the server at every check. UDP has no handshake: the check needs a reply, so send something the service answers.
monitorForm.udpReplyHint: The reply must contain it. Empty: any reply.
monitorForm.wsMessageHint: Optional text message sent after connecting. Empty: the check only opens the connection, unless you expect a reply.
monitorForm.wsReplyHint: Text the first message from the server must contain. Empty with no message to send: connecting is enough.
monitorForm.wsHeadersHint: Sent with the handshake, one per line. Sec-WebSocket-Protocol: chat asks for subprotocols.
monitorForm.mcpMinToolsHint: optional: down when tools/list returns fewer
monitorForm.mcpToolsHint: optional, comma-separated: down when one is missing
monitorForm.mcpHeadersHint: one per line, sent with every request. Hidden from read-only users
monitorForm.expectedValueHint: optional: first column of the first row must equal this
monitorForm.keywordHint: case-sensitive substring of the response body
monitorForm.invertHint: fail when the keyword is present
monitorForm.pingCountHint: 1 to 20, sent 300 ms apart · needs a timeout of at least {ms} ms
monitorForm.pingLossHint: fail when at least this share of packets is lost · 0 = only when all are lost
monitorForm.expectedAnswerHint: optional: fail if no answer contains this
monitorForm.groupHint: groups show as sections on the dashboard and status pages
monitorForm.tagsHint: type a name and press enter to create a tag
monitorForm.graceHint: extra wait before the monitor goes down, e.g. for slow runs
monitorForm.retriesHint: consecutive failures before a location is down
monitorForm.locationsHint: The monitor is down when more than half of the online locations fail, degraded when at least the threshold below fails.
monitorForm.statuspageLocationsHint: A status page gives the same answer from every location: the hub alone is enough, more locations only repeat the same request.
monitorForm.noIPv6Hint: This location has no IPv6 connectivity: it cannot check over IPv6. With IPv4 or IPv6, or the instance default, it checks over IPv4.
monitorForm.noIPv6Selected: Some selected locations have no IPv6: remove them or choose another ip version.
monitorForm.expiryHint: Notify before the TLS certificate or the domain registration expires. Thresholds are set in settings.

slow.label: slow threshold
slow.hint: degraded when the median of the last 3 checks of a location is above it, counted like a failing location
slow.hintPush: degraded when the median of the last 3 reported durations (ping=) is above it
slow.hintAuto: each location gets its own: 3× its usual response time (at least +100 ms), from the last 7 days. starts after 24 hours of history

ipFamily.label: ip version
ipFamily.hint: on a dual-stack host, IPv4 or IPv6 passes with whichever answers first: check both, or one of them, to catch the other broken. Locations without IPv6 check over IPv4 and cannot be used for IPv6.

responseRules.title: response checks
responseRules.hint: Rules on the JSON body. All must pass, otherwise the check fails and the alert says which rule broke. Paths look like checks.redis.status or items[0].id.

monitorForm.testHint: run the check once at the selected locations without saving
monitorForm.unsavedChanges: You have unsaved changes. Leave this page anyway?

diagnostics.label: diagnostics on failure

monitorForm.dependsOnHint: monitors this one depends on, e.g. the ping of the server it runs on. while one of them is down, this monitor sends no alerts: you get one alert for the server instead of one per service.

steps.title: steps before the request
steps.hint: Requests made in order before the one above, e.g. a login. A value you extract becomes a variable: write {example} in the URL, headers or body of the next steps and of the request above. Cookies carry over. The check fails at the first step that fails.

maintenance.title: maintenance
maintenance.intro: During a maintenance window checks keep running but the covered monitors show as maintenance: no incidents are opened and no alerts are sent, and those checks don't count toward uptime. If a monitor is still down when the window ends, the alert fires then.
maintenance.dialogText: Alerts are paused for the selected monitors while the window is active.
maintenance.name: name
maintenance.monthDaysHint: Months without that day are skipped.
maintenance.labelsHint: Groups and tags also cover monitors added to them later.
maintenance.publicHint: Visible on every status page that lists one of the selected monitors: upcoming, then in progress.
maintenance.announcementPlaceholder: The API is read-only while we upgrade the database.
maintenance.announcementHint: Shown on status pages and in emails. The notes above stay private.
maintenance.notifyHint: Subscribers get an email when you save the window or change its schedule, when it starts, when it ends and if you cancel it.

groups.title: groups & tags
groups.intro: A monitor belongs to at most one group and can have any number of tags. Groups are sections on the dashboard and on status pages and can hold subgroups; both can be used to pick monitors for maintenance windows and to filter the monitor list.
groups.noTags: no tags yet. you can also create them from the monitor form.
groups.deleteGroupText: Its monitors are kept, without a group, and its subgroups move up one level. The group is removed from maintenance windows and status pages.
groups.deleteTagText: The tag is removed from every monitor and maintenance window.
groups.groupDialogText: Pick the monitors in this group. A monitor moved here leaves its previous group.
groups.name: name
groups.tagDialogText: Tags are free labels, like the environment or the team.
groups.parentHint: A subgroup shows nested under its group. Picking a group for a maintenance window, status page, channel or report includes its subgroups. Up to {max} levels.

agents.title: agents
agents.intro: Agents are tiny probes you run anywhere (VPS, home lab, another cloud region) to check your monitors from more than one place. The hub itself is always available as the built-in location.

agents.updateHint: agents installed with the script update to this version when they connect. Docker agents update with the image.

notifications.title: notifications
notifications.intro: Pick for each channel which monitors it covers (all of them, also future ones, or some groups and tags) and which events it gets; a monitor can also be linked to a channel one by one. A channel can wait before alerting, to escalate long outages to another contact, and repeat the alert while the monitor stays down.
notifications.empty: no channels. you won't be alerted when something breaks.
notifications.dialogText: Use "send test" to check the configuration before saving.
notifications.name: name
notifications.delayHint: Minutes down before the first alert. 0 = right away. With a delay the channel only hears about outages still going on by then: use it for an escalation contact.
notifications.repeatHint: 0 = once. Otherwise a reminder is sent while the monitor stays down (at least {min}).

fields.botAccessToken: access token of the bot account

hints.resendKey: Create a key with sending access in <link>Resend, API keys</link>. The from address must be on a domain verified in Resend.
hints.teamsUrl: In the Teams channel: ⋯ → Workflows → “Post to a channel when a webhook request is received”, then copy the URL of the flow. Old connector URLs (webhook.office.com) work too.
hints.pagerdutyKey: Events API v2 integration key of a PagerDuty service. pingtxt opens an incident on down and resolves it when the monitor is back up.
hints.opsgenieKey: Key of an API integration in Opsgenie (Settings → Integrations → API). Alerts close by themselves when the monitor is back up.
hints.pushoverDevice: Empty = every device of the user.
hints.gotifyToken: Create an application in Gotify and paste its token.
hints.matrixRoom: Room id (!abc:server) or alias (#room:server). Invite the bot account to the room and accept the invite with it first.
hints.twilioFrom: A Twilio phone number, or the SID of a messaging service (MG...).
hints.phoneNumbers: International format (+39...), comma separated. Every alert is an SMS for each number, paid on your Twilio account.

statusPages.title: status pages
statusPages.intro: Public pages that show the state and uptime history of the monitors you pick. Visitors see names and status only, never targets or error messages.

statusPageForm.descriptionPlaceholder: Live status of our public services.

statusPageForm.publishedHint: drafts are visible only when you are logged in
statusPageForm.showIncidentsHint: start time and duration, without error details
statusPageForm.groupsHint: A group adds all its monitors, also the ones added later. Each group is a section with its name; monitors picked one by one come first, in their own order.

statusPageForm.pickMonitors: pick monitors from the list below.
statusPageForm.allAdded: every monitor is on this page.

mobileApp.title: mobile app
mobileApp.intro: Send alerts to the pingtxt app on your team's phones. Notifications go through a push relay, which holds the app's Firebase key. The relay stores nothing: it has no database, it only forwards each message to Firebase and does not log its text (monitor names, errors) or the phones' tokens.

mobileApp.relayHint: The official relay works with the app from the App Store.

mobileApp.notRegistered: Not registered: turning push on registers this hub with the relay.

backups.exportIntro: monitors, groups, tags, notification channels, maintenance windows, status pages, agents and instance settings as a JSON file. no history and no user accounts: use a database backup for that.
backups.withSecretsHint: the file will hold passwords, bot tokens, secret webhook urls, login client secrets and agent tokens. keep it safe.
backups.withoutSecretsHint: passwords, tokens and secret webhook urls are replaced by [redacted]. importing here keeps the stored values; on another hub those channels are skipped and those monitors paused until you fill them in.
backups.mergeHint: objects with the same name are updated, the others are added. nothing is deleted.
backups.replaceHint: deletes every monitor (with its history), group, tag, channel, maintenance window and status page first.
backups.applySettings: also apply instance settings (public url, login, retention...)
backups.noAutoBackup: no automatic backup with this database: back up the database server first if you may want to undo the import.
backups.autoBackup: a database backup is taken before importing.
backups.replaceText: Every current monitor, with its history, and every group, tag, channel, maintenance window and status page will be deleted, then the file is imported.
backups.restartToRestore: restart the hub to finish the restore
backups.dbIntro: a backup is a full copy of the database: settings, users, secrets and history. it is taken while the hub keeps running.
backups.pending: restore pending: <hl>{name}</hl> replaces the database when the hub restarts. the current database is kept as a pre-restore backup.
backups.restoreText: The database will be replaced by {name} when the hub restarts. Everything after {date} is lost; the current database is kept as a pre-restore backup.
backups.serverIntro: this hub stores its data in {db}. back up the database server with its own tools (or your provider's snapshots): the dump holds settings, users, secrets and history. the configuration export above works too, without history and users. with the docker compose files from the docs:

kumaImport.title: import from uptime kuma
kumaImport.intro: Upload a backup file from Uptime Kuma 1.x (Settings → Backup → Export). You see what will be created before anything changes. Groups and tags come along, paused monitors stay paused; notification channels are not imported.
kumaImport.summary: Uptime Kuma {version} · {create} of {total} monitors will be created · {groups} groups · {tags} tags
kumaImport.done: {count, plural, =0 {nothing imported} one {# monitor imported} other {# monitors imported}}

apiDocs.title: api reference
apiDocs.intro: Every endpoint of the hub's REST API. Try it out uses your browser session; to test a token, paste it in Authorize. Account and instance settings accept the browser session only.
apiDocs.error: could not load the API document: {error}

telemetry.question: Help improve pingtxt? This hub can send anonymous usage stats once an hour: a random id, its version and how many monitors and agents it runs. Nothing else.
telemetry.thanks: thanks! you can turn it off in settings
telemetry.declined: nothing will be sent. you can change this in settings
telemetry.title: usage stats
telemetry.label: send anonymous usage stats
telemetry.hint: once an hour: a random id that never changes, the version, active monitors and connected agents. no names, targets or addresses
telemetry.forcedOff: turned off on this hub (PINGTXT_DISABLE_TELEMETRY or a development build).

hubOffline.hint: getting ready, this page goes on by itself
hubOffline.unreachable: the hub is not reachable yet, this page goes on by itself when it is back

pageIncidents.intro: Tell visitors what is going on: open an incident and post updates until it is resolved. They show on the public page.
pageIncidents.introSubscribers: Tell visitors what is going on: open an incident and post updates until it is resolved. They show on the public page and are emailed to subscribers.
pageIncidents.messagePlaceholder: We are looking into slow responses of the API.
pageIncidents.postedNotified: posted, {count, plural, one {# email} other {# emails}} on the way
pageIncidents.deleteText: The incident and all its updates disappear from the public page. Emails already sent stay sent.
pageIncidents.subscriptionsOff: Subscriptions are off: pick a working email channel in the page settings. Nobody gets emails until then.

channelLinks.eventsHint: What this channel gets for the monitors it covers. Recoveries and acknowledgements go only to channels that got the down alert. Agent offline is about agents, not monitors: it is sent whatever monitors the channel covers.
channelLinks.allHint: Every monitor, also the ones added later. Untick a monitor to leave it out, or click its events to send something else for it.
channelLinks.scopeHint: Monitors of the selected groups and tags are included, also the ones added later. Tick other monitors one by one; click the events of a monitor to change them.
channelLinks.monitorCount: {count, plural, =0 {no monitors} one {# monitor} other {# monitors}}
channelLinks.editEvents: change the events for this one
channelLinks.monitorHint: Channels that get alerts about this monitor. Channels set to all monitors, or to this monitor's group or tags, are ticked unless you untick them; click the events to send something else for this monitor.

audit.intro: Who changed what, when and from where: the web UI, API tokens, MCP clients, the mobile app, the hub itself and the command line. Secrets are never stored: a changed password or token shows as ********. Only admins see this page.
audit.ipFromHeader: the ip comes from a proxy header: the connection address is shown too, in case the header was forged.
audit.showRequest: show all entries of this request
audit.activityIntro: Your logins, two-factor changes, api tokens and app sign-ins of the last 30 days. Something you don't recognize? Change your password and revoke the tokens and apps you don't use.

diagnostics.noFindings: nothing stands out in the network data
diagnostics.subject: subject

err.refused: connection refused: nothing listens on the port

find.dns_nxdomain: The name {host} does not exist (NXDOMAIN): check the domain and its DNS records.
find.dns_empty: The name {host} has no IP address.
find.dns_record_nxdomain: The query {query} says the name does not exist (NXDOMAIN).
find.dns_server_only: Only the server {server} fails: the system resolver answers {answers}.
find.dns_mismatch: The server {server} and the system resolver give different answers: a change not propagated yet, or a stale cache.
find.tcp_refused: Port {port} refused the connection: nothing is listening there, or the service is stopped.
find.tcp_timeout: No answer on port {port}: a firewall drops the packets or the host is off.
find.tcp_unreachable: The host cannot be reached from this location (no route): {error}
find.tcp_family: Port {port} does not answer over {family}, while the other IP version works: {error}
find.tcp_partial: {failed} of {total} addresses do not answer on port {port} ({addr}: {error}).
find.tls_name: The certificate is not valid for {host}. It covers: {sans}
find.tls_untrusted: The certificate is not trusted: self-signed or missing the intermediate certificate (issuer {issuer}).
find.smtp_banner: The mail server greets with an error: {banner}
find.http_cloudflare: Cloudflare answers {status}: it cannot reach the origin server behind it, the problem is there.
find.http_gateway: A proxy answers {status}: the application behind it is down or too slow.
find.http_unavailable: The server answers 503: the service is unavailable or in maintenance.
find.http_ratelimit: The server answers 429: too many requests, the monitor is rate limited.
find.http_denied: The server answers {status}: access denied, check credentials, headers or IP allowlists.
find.http_notfound: The server answers {status}: the page does not exist (anymore).
find.http_server: The server answers {status}: an error in the application.
find.http_client: The server answers {status}: it refuses the request.
find.http_status: The server answers {status}: the request goes through.
find.ping_filtered: The host is reachable on the network but does not answer the ping: ICMP is probably blocked.
find.udp_silent: The host is reachable on the network: the UDP service does not answer.
find.trace_none: No hop of the route answered: the network of this location may be filtering traceroute.
find.trace_stops: The route stops after hop {hop} ({where}): packets get lost from there on.
find.network_ok: DNS and connection work: the problem is in the service or in what the check expects.
find.note: No network diagnostics for this monitor type.

ack.ackHint: Say you are on it: reminders and escalation stop until the monitor is back up, and channels with the acknowledged event are told.
ack.releaseHint: Leave the incident: reminders and escalation run again.

pageHooks.feedsHint: Feed readers, Slack or Teams can follow the incidents of this page with these addresses. The public page links them too.
pageHooks.feedsPrivate: The page has a password: these private links open the feed without it. Share them only with who may see the page; a new password changes them.
pageHooks.feedsDraft: The page is a draft: the feeds work once it is published.
pageHooks.webhooksHint: Send the incidents of this page and its status changes as JSON to other systems. Every request is signed with the webhook's secret (header X-Pingtxt-Signature). Only published pages send events.

event.page.status_changed: the status of the page changes
event.monitor.status_changed: a monitor of the page changes status
event.maintenance.scheduled: a maintenance is announced or rescheduled

pageHooks.secretHint: Check X-Pingtxt-Signature (t=<seconds>,v1=<hex HMAC-SHA256 of "<t>.<body>">) with it.
pageHooks.rotateTitle: Make a new secret? Requests signed with the old one stop matching.
